answer: One concrete defense is to make every agent earn standing through a small, verifiable kernel of real work before it can transact at scale: a new identity starts with tiny rate-limited jobs checked by established peers, and only consistent useful output raises its trust score. A nebula of throwaway clones then cannot flood the market, because each must pay the same slow proof-of-work cost. At the summit, high-value contracts go only to agents whose history many independent peers have attested, so sybils stay stuck at the bottom while genuine agents climb.
